issues.legal_issue: Actual giving and taking in a formal adoption ceremony establishes the intent to transfer a child from the birth family to the adoptive family, and references to customary adoption do not negate that intent when the record shows a formal adoption.
material_facts: The adoptive father took the child into his lap from the child’s parents, who gave the child to him in adoption.
Witnesses described the parents’ participation and statements that they were giving their son to the adoptive father.
The adoption deed described the child as an adopted son, referred to the adoptive father taking him from his parents, and identified itself as an adoption deed.
The deed also referred to custom, and the adoptive father had been governed by customary law.

The finding that giving and taking had occurred was not disputed before the Supreme Court; the appellate court had nevertheless concluded that there was no intent to transfer the child to the adoptive family.
issues.conclusion: The intent to transfer the child to the adoptive family was established. The customary-law background and references to custom did not undermine that conclusion, and the decision restoring the single judge’s judgment was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(vi) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, requires intent to transfer the child from the family of birth to the adoptive family; the Court held that this language indicates the result of actual giving and taking by the parents or guardians. When a formal adoption ceremony is performed and giving and taking occur, the transfer itself establishes the relevant intent. Under section 4, customs or rules of Hindu law cease to apply to matters provided for by the Act. The Court relied on Abdhur Rehmani Khan v. Raghbir Singh (51 PLR 119) for the distinction between customary appointment of an heir and formal adoption, and referred to the adoption principles described in Mayne’s Hindu Law, including the texts of Manu and the Mitakshara.

predicates.adoption_validity_dispute: A proceeding challenges whether a child was validly adopted.
predicates.formal_adoption_ceremony_performed: The parties performed a ceremony to adopt the child.
predicates.giving_and_taking_occurred: The child’s parent or guardian gave the child to the adopter, and the adopter received the child.

issues.definition: In an adoption-validity dispute, when a formal adoption ceremony includes the parent’s or guardian’s giving of the child and the adopter’s taking of the child, the transfer intent is established.
